ananya.name: Dr. Ananya

Shoulder-length black hair tied in a low bun with a few loose strands, slim build, small gold stud earrings, a stethoscope worn around her neck (never in use) in every scene where she wears the white coat (manga supplement, from the accepted reference sheet).

script.style: Full-colour, approachable Indian slice-of-life manga. Clean confident line art with varied line weight, soft flat cel shading, warm natural daylight, restrained blue and teal accents, simple readable backgrounds. Expressive but natural faces, precise hands. No photorealism, no glossy gradients, no surface microtexture. Absolutely no text, letters, logos, numbers, speech bubbles or captions inside the artwork; device screens show only abstract blank blocks and simple icons.
script.continuity: Keep Dr. Ananya, Meera, Ravi, the Nurse, Mr. Raman and Priya identical to their canonical reference sheets in face traits, hair, build, skin tone and clothing for the whole comic. Device screens never show readable text or real personal data. Page 8 panels 2-3 (08-2, 08-3) are a future vision: soft pale-blue vignette border and lighter, airy palette so they never read as current features.

pages.scan: Panel 1 (full-width top, daytime outside the clinic): caption top-left 'A busy day at Dr. Ananya's clinic.' A doctor in a white coat, teal kurta and stethoscope, hair in a bun with loose strands, waves an elderly woman in a lilac sari into the clinic. Two patients wait on metal chairs on the right, seen from behind. Panel 2 (lower left, front desk): a receptionist in a blue patterned kurta with a long braid is on the desk phone and writing in a ledger, looking flustered, with sweat drop and stress marks. Left balloon 'Appointments, patient details, follow-ups...', then right balloon 'I wish everything were easier to manage!' Both tails point to the receptionist. Patients' heads are in the foreground. Panel 3 (lower right): the doctor stands thinking, hand on chin, with the receptionist small in the background. Balloon 'Our time belongs with patients. Let's make the rest simpler.' Its tail points to the doctor.
pages.observation: Reading order is clear: top panel, then lower left, then lower right. In panel 2 the two balloons read naturally left then right, and both clearly belong to the receptionist. The panel 3 line 'Our time belongs with patients' reads a little awkwardly ('belongs with' rather than 'belongs to' or 'should be with'). The panel 3 tail ends right at the doctor's hair and cheek. The panel 2 left tail ends at the top of the receptionist's hair. Neither hides the face. The doctor's costume (teal kurta, white coat, stethoscope, bun) and the receptionist's (blue kurta, braid) are consistent between panels. Text is legible.

pages.scan: Panel 1 (full-width top, sunset through the window): caption top-left 'The clinic begins its Welbuk onboarding.' Label top-right 'WELBUK PRACTICE for the clinic'. The doctor, seen from behind over her shoulder, types on a laptop showing a step-progress form. Panel 2 (middle left): the doctor, hand on chin, smiles at the laptop. Balloon 'We can organise our clinic workflow here.' Its tail points to the doctor. Panel 3 (middle right): the receptionist stands holding up a phone with a calendar app. Balloon 'And our team can use tools suited to each staff role.' Its tail points to the receptionist. Label bottom 'WELBUK CARE for clinic staff'. Panel 4 (full-width bottom): the doctor at her desk raises a fist, cheerful. Balloon 'One team. Better coordination.' Its tail points to the doctor. The receptionist stands at right holding the phone and smiling, silent.
pages.observation: Reading order is clear: top, middle left, middle right, bottom. 'And our team...' follows naturally on from the doctor's line. Time change: page 1 was daylight on a busy day, and here the window shows sunset with no time caption, so the evening jump is shown only by the lighting. Continuity: in panel 4 the doctor's hair looks looser and fuller around the face, and her face looks younger and rounder than in panels 1-2 and page 1, so she is slightly less recognisable. The receptionist's braid and kurta stay consistent. Lettering contacts: the bottom edge of the panel 1 caption box sits right on top of the doctor's hair. The 'WELBUK CARE' label covers the receptionist's lower dress and comes close to her hand at her hip. The panel 4 balloon's left edge and tail sit right against the doctor's hair and cheek. The panel 2 tail ends at the doctor's hair. Text is legible.

pages.scan: Panel 1 (top left): caption 'A later morning: patients can always check in at the front desk.' An elderly man with glasses and a cane talks to the smiling receptionist at the desk. A check-in kiosk with a QR code is at left. Panel 2 (top right, outside the entrance): caption 'Some check in ahead on the Welbuk Health app.' A young woman in a coral patterned kurta with a ponytail and a navy shoulder bag taps a phone showing a calendar and check mark. Panel 3 (middle left): caption 'Ravi scans the QR code at the door.' A bearded man in a sage-green shirt with a brown shoulder bag and wristwatch scans the kiosk QR code with his phone. The receptionist, elderly man and coral woman are in the background. Panel 4 (middle right): caption 'A short form on his own phone, shared with consent.' Close-up of Ravi's hands holding a phone with a form and a check mark. Panel 5 (full-width bottom): caption 'Every check-in gets a slot on the screen.' Wall-screen label 'A-10 · A-11 · A-12'. The elderly man, the coral woman and Ravi sit side by side in the waiting room, silently looking up at the screen.
pages.observation: Reading order is clear: row by row, left to right. The time jump is handled by the caption 'A later morning'. This is the first time Ravi is named, and only in a caption. The coral woman and elderly man are never named, but they work as examples. Panel 5 does not show which slot is Ravi's. Seating order suggests A-12, and page 4 confirms it, but on this page it is inferred. Lettering contacts: the panel 3 caption's right and bottom edges overlap the top-left of Ravi's hair. The panel 4 caption's right edge touches Ravi's hair and forehead. The panel 2 caption bottom sits just above the woman's hair. Props are consistent: Ravi's brown bag and watch, the coral woman's navy bag, the elderly man's cane. Text is legible.

pages.scan: Panel 1 (full-width top): caption top-left 'Soon, his slot comes up.' Wall-screen label top-right 'NOW · A-12'. Ravi stands up from the blue waiting chairs with his bag on his shoulder, looking at the screen and smiling. The receptionist is at the desk at right, silent. Panel 2 (lower left): caption 'A quick vitals check first.' A nurse in lilac scrubs with short wavy hair and an ID lanyard puts a blood-pressure cuff on Ravi's arm and a pulse oximeter on his finger. pages.observation: Reading order is clear: top, lower left, lower right. 'NOW · A-12' confirms Ravi's slot from page 3. The nurse is a new, unnamed character, but her role is clear from the scrubs and the action. The waiting room in panel 1 looks much emptier than the full row of page 3, panel 5, which is a minor continuity point. Lettering contacts: the nurse's balloon tail sits right on the top of her hair. The 'RAVI · READY' label covers most of the tablet screen and its right edge touches the doctor's right-hand fingers. The label breaks awkwardly as 'RAVI ·' / 'READY'. pages.observation: Reading order is clear: top, middle, lower left, lower right. Ravi's answer to 'Tell me what brings you in' ('I've been feeling tired lately') comes two panels later, after the consent exchange. That is readable, but the reply is delayed and could feel disconnected. Panel 2's balloons are close together and in the right order, though the 'Yes, I agree.' tail crosses a long empty span to a very small Ravi. Panel 2 figures are small, so faces are hard to read. Panels 1 and 3 are dense with labels. The SOAP NOTES label is long and text-heavy for one panel. Lettering contacts: the panel 1 tail ends near the doctor's chin and mouth. The panel 3 tail ends at Ravi's ear and hair. The SOAP NOTES label covers most of the laptop screen except the mic icon. The panel 4 caption's lower-right corner touches the back of Ravi's head. Ravi's shirt, watch and bag are consistent. Text is legible.

pages.observation: Reading order is clear: top, then bottom. Abrupt topic change: after Ravi says he feels tired (page 5), the first panel cuts to a planner for dentists, eye doctors and paediatricians, none of which relates to his complaint. A reader may wonder whether Ravi is seeing a dentist or eye doctor, or whether this is a product aside. Ravi's tiredness is not followed up on this page or later. Lettering contacts: the balloon tail ends at the doctor's hair on the right side of her head. The PLAN OF CARE label covers the laptop screen and overlaps part of the doctor's coat and the lower stethoscope tubing. In panel 1 the 'Paediatrician' label overlaps the edge of the screen and keyboard area. The doctor and Ravi are consistent. Text is legible.

pages.observation: Reading order is clear: top left, top right, middle, bottom. Abrupt scene changes: from waving goodbye at the clinic (page 7) straight to Ravi on a train, then a different doctor and city, then a home with a woman and child, then back in front of the clinic. Apart from the general 'Tomorrow' caption, nothing frames these as future or imagined. The older doctor, the woman and the boy are new and unexplained (presumably Ravi's family, but it is not stated). 'Tomorrow' could be read literally as the next day. The panel 2 and 3 'vision' framing is clear only from the labels. Lettering contacts: the panel 2 bottom caption covers the older doctor's lower torso and coat just below his gesturing hand. In panel 3, the caption's right edge comes close to Ravi's shoulder and arm. In panel 4, the bottom caption covers the receptionist's feet and lower hem and touches the hem and leg of the doctor's coat. The top-right label sits right beside Ravi's head and raised hand without covering his face. The panel 1 caption sits close to Ravi's hair. The main cast's costumes, braid, bun, Ravi's bag and the receptionist's phone are consistent. Text is legible.
